Given: $V_m = 9\text{ V}$, $V_1 = 5\text{ V}$, $V_2 = 6\text{ V}$, and diodes are ideal.

1. **Analyze Diode 1 ($D_1$) branch:** Connected with DC voltage source $V_1 = 5\text{ V}$ in series. Since it is forward biased when input voltage exceeds $5\text{ V}$, $D_1$ conducts when $V_i > 5\text{ V}$, clamping the output $V_0$ at $5\text{ V}$.
2. **Analyze Diode 2 ($D_2$) branch:** Connected with DC voltage source $V_2 = 6\text{ V}$. It conducts when the input drops below $-6\text{ V}$ (or relative polarity limits), clamping negative excursions.
3. **Output Waveform ($V_0$):** The input sinusoid $V_i$ swings between $+9\text{ V}$ and $-9\text{ V}$. 
   - When $V_i$ exceeds $5\text{ V}$, the top diode clips the output at **$+5\text{ V}$**.
   - When $V_i$ is between $-6\text{ V}$ and $+5\text{ V}$, $V_0$ follows the input $V_i$.
   - Thus, the output waveform is a clipped sinusoid clipped symmetrically or at $+5\text{ V}$ on the positive peak.
proTip: Always check the polarity of the DC sources and diodes to determine clipping thresholds accurately.
